title: Can and Can't for Ability and Permission
summary: Learn how to talk about what you are able to do. You will also learn how to ask for and give permission.

sections.p: We use the word 'can' to talk about things we know how to do. This is called ability. The word 'can' is the same for all people: I can, you can, he can, she can, it can, we can, they can. After 'can', we use a simple action word like swim, cook, or speak. It is very easy to use and helps you share your skills with friends.

ex.en: I can speak a little English.
ex.mean: I know how to speak a little English.
She has the ability to swim fast.
Do you know how to cook dinner?

sections.p: When we cannot do something, we use 'can't'. 'Can't' means 'cannot'. We use it for things we do not know how to do or things that are not allowed. Just like 'can', the word 'can't' stays the same for everyone. It is a great way to say no politely or explain your limits.

ex.mean: I do not know how to play the guitar.
It is impossible for cats to fly.

ex.en: He can't come to the party.
ex.mean: He is not able to come to the party.

sections.p: We also use 'can' to ask if we are allowed to do something. This is called permission. When you want to do something in a public place or at someone's house, start your question with 'Can I...'. People will answer with 'Yes, you can' or 'No, you can't'. This is very useful for daily life.

ex.en: Can I open the window, please?
ex.mean: Am I allowed to open the window?
You have permission to do it.

tip: Remember that 'can' never changes! We never add an 's' to it, so we always say 'He can', not 'He cans'.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct word for ability

quiz.en: Birds can fly, but fish ___ fly.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct question for permission

quiz.en: Can she speak Spanish? Yes, she ___.
He ___ play the piano. He is a great musician.

quiz.ask: Choose the correct answer for a negative question
quiz.en: Can I park here? No, you ___.
